x: John Gladwin won the 800m in 2.1.4 and received good backing up in the other events from Pat Lyttle, Alister Horton and Raymond Young. After three meetings the Youths were third and the Seniors fourth.
A word of consolation to Alister Horton who suffered from car sickness and couldn't run. Youths: 1.M.King (W.Corn.) 16:43; 5.D.North 17:17; 20.J.Gladwin 17:45; 46.M.Waller 18:14; 61.

Alister Horton continued his steady improvement to finish within 26 seconds of Gerry. New member Andy Jones running in his first race for Belgrave finished in 45th place, but will need to match the training schedules of our other youngsters if he is to fulfil his potential.

With Dave North unable to run the Bels Youth team looked considerably weaker than the winning Luton one. First year youths, Gerry Sexton and Alister Horton presented Colin Pearson with the difficult task of deciding the running order.
…orking hard to hold a fierce pace. At 2 miles John Gladwin was 3rd, Dave 4th, Mark Waller 6th and Gerry Sexton 8th with Alister Horton backing up in the 20's.…

In very windy conditions Alister Horton confirmed rumours of his improved training by finishing the first 1¾ mile leg in 4th position; Stuart Paton steamed round in the fastest time of the day to take Bels into the lead.
Alister Horton (6) and Paul Richley (12) battle for the lead in the Surreys.

Paul Richley who was within 3 seconds of Stu Paton's course record and Alister Horton who at the last minute ran to complete the Youth's team - his first run since being knocked off his bike in France by a speeding car.

Without John Gladwin and Mark Sinclair or John Searle and with Olly Foote not yet able to score for us it was left to the 'old firm' of Paton, Richley and North to form the spear-head of our scoring four with Alistair Horton rising to the occasion with an excellent run to close our team in.
On the Country, our Junior Team of Alistair Horton, Stuart Paton, Paul Richley and Mark Waller retained the Junior Team Race in the Surrey Country C.C.
New member Oliver Foote (52) follows Alister Horton (49) who shields second place man David North.

…to finish a close 3rd to winner Chris Carter who later was to gain 10th place in the Junior International at Gateshead. Alister Horton ran well to be the first London runner home in 77th place having qualified by coming second in the London Schools Champs.…
